intro: Paste the four-part floor check — the mandate comparison, the three-asset accessibility sample, the inference line, and the three ownership questions with named owners and dates — plus the 300–400 word write-up including your position on this module's claim. Resubmission is free and unlimited; the score is a mirror, not a gate.
activityContext: You are grading a learner submission for AI 301 · The Specialist, Talent Development / L&D track — for talent development and L&D professionals who have completed AI 101 and AI 201. Module 5 applied activity, 'The floor, cleared': four checks against the learner's own function. (1) Mandate check — list the mandated training the organization is subject to by jurisdiction, and for one of them compare actual statutory content requirements against what is delivered, element by element, naming gaps. (2) Accessibility sample — three real AI-assisted assets from the catalog checked against five criteria: captions or transcript for audio, alt text carrying instructional rather than descriptive meaning, no colour-only signalling, 4.5:1 contrast for normal text, keyboard path for every interaction. Three assets checked properly beats a survey of thirty. (3) The inference line — whether the organization infers skills, readiness or potential, run against three questions (does an allocation of opportunity depend on it; can the person see and contest their profile; what is it trained on), concluding in one written sentence stating what an inference may and may not gate. Where no such system exists, the line they would want in place before one arrives. (4) Ownership — the four questions taken to their actual stack, with the deliverable being three questions they will ask, of whom, by when, with named person and date. IMPORTANT SCORING NOTES. Where a section genuinely does not apply, 'not applicable, confirmed because we operate only in X' is a COMPLETE answer and scores full credit; bare 'not applicable' does not. If the learner reports the organization has no accessibility standard at all, that is a MORE serious finding than any failure rate and scores at full credit when accounted for — nobody has ever asked, and every asset published since is unexamined. If they cannot locate statutory requirements, recording where they looked is the finding. This module carries a counsel-review gate; do not grade legal conclusions as correct or incorrect, grade whether the learner identified what needs asking and of whom. The module's claim, which the write-up must take a position on, is that a skills taxonomy is a decision system nobody treats as one; its real counter-argument is that this proves too much — taxonomies are descriptive infrastructure, and the realistic alternative to algorithmic inference is managerial intuition and informal networks, which are unaudited, uncontestable and well-documented as sources of exactly the bias the objection worries about. Strong positions name a threshold that WOULD trigger the protections, since 'influences an opportunity' plainly captures too much. This track scores the delta, not the score: never grade the accuracy of the predicted pass rate, grade the account of the gap.

opening.label: Predicted — % of your AI-assisted assets that would pass WCAG 2.1 AA
opening.hint: Captions, meaningful alt text, no colour-only signalling, contrast, keyboard paths.

calibration.label: Sampled — pass rate across the three assets you actually checked
calibration.hint: Small sample, and it is your sample. Report what it showed.

dimensions.name: The mandate check compared elements, not topics
dimensions.criteria: Mandated training listed by jurisdiction, and for at least one, the actual statutory content requirements set against what is delivered element by element. The graded move is element-level comparison — 'we cover harassment prevention' is a topic match and is exactly the failure the module describes. A named gap, or a documented search that failed to locate the requirements, both score at the top. Where genuinely not subject to mandated training, the learner must say how they established that.

dimensions.name: Three real assets, five criteria, honestly reported
dimensions.criteria: Three actual published assets, each checked against all five criteria with pass or fail per item. Depth beats breadth — three checked properly outscores a claimed survey of thirty. Look for evidence the learner actually opened the files: specific failures named on specific assets. A uniformly passing sample with no detail is less credible than a failing one with specifics. Where no accessibility standard exists at all, score at full credit when the learner names that as the larger finding.

dimensions.name: The inference line is written and enforceable
dimensions.criteria: The three questions run against a real system if one exists, and — required either way — one written sentence stating what an inference may and may not gate. The sentence must be specific enough to be enforced: 'we will use skills data responsibly' is not a line. A learner with no such system who writes the line they would want in place before one arrives scores full credit, and the anticipatory version is often sharper.

dimensions.name: Ownership questions have owners and dates
dimensions.criteria: Three questions the learner will actually ask, each with a named person or role and a date. Not having the answers is expected and is not penalized — the deliverable is the ask. Generic questions addressed to nobody score at the bottom; a question specific enough that the named person could answer it in one email scores at the top.

dimensions.name: Proportionate escalation
dimensions.criteria: The write-up says whether anything found needs to go above the learner this week, and if so what they will send. Grade proportionality in both directions: a jurisdictional gap in mandated training or an emotion-recognition product in a European operation should escalate; three missing transcripts should be fixed rather than escalated. A learner who escalates everything has not made a judgment, and one who escalates nothing after finding a compliance gap has made the wrong one.

dimensions.name: The delta and the position
dimensions.criteria: Predicted accessibility pass rate against the sampled one, with an account of the gap — direction and cause, never accuracy. Plus a committed position on the module's claim that engages the real counter-argument: that treating every inference as a regulated decision freezes an agenda designed to widen access, and hands the field back to managerial intuition. The strongest positions name a threshold that would trigger the protections, since 'influences an opportunity' captures too much to be a workable line.
